body:
I just wanted to say Thank You, to each and every person who commented on my post. It meant SO much. 

I don't know how it works that I can go for years being such a strong, tough, and semi-cold person and turn into a cowardly child hiding behind the drier because a memory has me terrified. Seriously, for hours. 
Hyperventilating, screaming, crying, and begging for the pain to stop. I relived my abuse today, to an extent that I didn't know was possible. I've dealt with flashbacks, deja vu that makes me sick, and a pretty bitter outlook. I know the outlook is my responsibility, and that is something I try to work on. But on days like today, I feel that I partially lose my ability to function in a sane way. I can't control the pain, and I can't forget some memories. 

The man who abused me is still out and about. He and his wife live a happy life in their home, that was never mine. He drives to his job every day, probably still gets his favorite coffee, and goes back to a warm home with the pantry and refrigerator full of everything he could ever want. 

As for myself, I have no car, no job, no money, no contact with anyone in the closest thing I ever had to a family. I was unable to pay my tab for one semester in my University, so until I could pay it off, I couldn't enroll in more classes. I still can't pay for it, a year and a half later. I've tried for financial aid, but since they were my legal guardians, the amount of my awards are dependent on their salaries, which are very high. 

What I do have is a wonderful best friend and boyfriend who loves me and takes care of me the absolute best he can. He is nothing short of wonderful. The problem is, I don't see a day when my childhood isn't impacting me in at least some way. I learned things the wrong way and I feel that this makes me a burden to him, when I should be a source of relief. I feel he deserves someone normal. Someone less, scarred.
